core_obligations: Compare each topology with the structure sheaf: for tau one of the topologies of the section, apply the inverse-function/cohomology identification to get H^1_tau(X, G_m) = H^1_tau(X, O_tau^*) = Pic(O_tau), where O_tau is the structure sheaf of the site (Sch/X)_tau (proof lines 2511-2521).

Discard the topology in the Picard group: an invertible O_tau-module is in particular a quasi-coherent O_tau-module, and quasi-coherent modules on the big site agree with quasi-coherent modules on X, so Pic(O_tau) = Pic(X); the author cites both the general comparison theorem and the more precise descent proposition (proof lines 2521-2525).

Assemble the chain: since tau was arbitrary among the topologies considered, all the groups H^1_tau(X, G_m) are canonically identified with Pic(X), and the last identification with H^1(X, O_X^*) is obtained in the same way (proof lines 2525-2526).
proof_roadmap: For each topology tau, use the standard description of H^1 of the multiplicative group as the first cohomology of the sheaf of units, hence as Picard groups of the structure sheaf of the site (proof lines 2511-2521).
Identify Picard groups of the structure sheaf with Pic(X) through quasi-coherence of invertible modules and the comparison of quasi-coherent modules across topologies (proof lines 2521-2525).
Conclude the chain of identifications for every topology at once, including the last one with H^1(X, O_X^*) (proof lines 2525-2526).
difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts a chain of canonical identifications H^1_{fppf}(X, G_m) = H^1_{syntomic}(X, G_m) = H^1_{smooth}(X, G_m) = H^1_etale(X, G_m) = H^1_{Zar}(X, G_m) = Pic(X) = H^1(X, O_X^*) for every scheme X (statement lines 2499-2507). The proof does not repeat the argument for each topology; it lets tau run over all the topologies considered in the big-and-small section and shows in one stroke that H^1_tau(X, G_m) = H^1_tau(X, O_tau^*) = Pic(O_tau) = Pic(X), where the middle step replaces the sheaf of units by the structure sheaf and the last step uses that invertible modules are quasi-coherent and that quasi-coherent modules are insensitive to the choice of topology (proof lines 2511-2525). What makes this short proof work is the recourse to the more precise descent proposition for quasi-coherent modules. The claim is H2: one uniform argument, three citations.
